facts.title: Neuron parts and signal direction
facts.claim: A neuron has dendrites, a soma, one axon, and axon terminals. Information flows dendrite → soma → axon → terminal.

facts.title: Myelin sheath and nodes
facts.claim: Myelin is a lipid-rich sheath made by glial cells. Gaps in the sheath are nodes of Ranvier; myelin speeds conduction.

facts.title: Threshold and the action potential
facts.claim: A stimulus must reach threshold before an action potential fires. At threshold, voltage-gated Na⁺ channels open; the spike peaks and then repolarises.

facts.title: All-or-none and one-way conduction
facts.claim: Action potentials are all-or-none: stronger stimuli increase frequency, not amplitude. The refractory period keeps the signal one-way; myelinated axons use saltatory conduction.
